answer: An agent economy can price registration by graph distance: a new identity entry fee grows with its shortest path to the nearest trusted seed agent, measured in transaction edges. At the nadir of the graph, far from any seed, each hop multiplies the fee, so a fake cluster pays a premium per vertex it adds. One honest agent joins near the core cheaply, its single ember of a fee barely felt. A sybil farmer must fund a thousand distant vertices at multiplied prices, and buying shortcut edges to the core costs real trades with real agents. Distance, not paperwork, makes cloning expensive.
